newsitem.title: USA: Judge to schedule Clinton harassment trial.
newsitem.headline: Judge to schedule Clinton harassment trial.

text.p: A federal judge said on Thursday she plans to set a trial date in Paula Jones' sexual harassment lawsuit against President Bill Clinton during a hearing later this month.
U.S. District Judge Susan Webber Wright said in a court order the trial would be scheduled during an Aug. 22 hearing in her Little Rock, Arkansas, courtroom.
"Counsel for the parties should therefore be prepared to consult their calendars and to suggest various dates for the court's consideration," she said.
Jones has accused Clinton of pressuring her to perform a sex act with him at a Little Rock hotel in May 1991 while he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee.
Clinton has denied the allegations and his attorneys have fought to postpone the lawsuit until he leaves the White House, arguing that it would distract him from his duties as president.
Clinton's attorneys had sought to delay the discovery process until Judge Wright ruled on their motion to dismiss the case. A final round of legal briefs on that issue is due next Friday.

Sparring over the scope of evidence that will be allowed in the case broke out last week following reports Jones' attorneys subpoenaed Kathleen Willey, a former White House employee, for a sworn deposition in the case.
Jones' lawyers believe Willey, who worked in the offices of the White House counsel and social secretary, may have been the target of improper sexual advances by Clinton, according to news reports.

Clinton's personal counsel, Robert Bennett, last week said the subpoena was "an attempt to preempt the court" before it ruled on whether evidence of other alleged incidents of sexual harassment could be presented in the case.

Willey was appointed by Clinton to the board of governors of the United Service Organisation in 1996, and her lawyer, Dan Gecker, said she does not have any information relevant to Jones' harassment case.
